inputs.text: Organizers say 8 million people joined more than 3,300 “No Kings” events across all 50 states—about one million more than in October. There’s no official count, so that figure should be treated as an estimate, not proof that everyone agrees. But dismissing mass protest because it isn’t a vote misses the point: peaceful public dissent is one way people hold power accountable between elections. Invoking “law and tradition” to silence protest can protect the status quo, especially when institutions fail to hear people who are already politically marginalized. A loud protest doesn’t govern the country, but neither should those in power mistake their authority for the public’s consent.
